turns.input: Explain why the daytime sky usually looks blue. I want the actual explanation.
turns.speech: Sunlight contains all colours of visible light, and each travels as a different wavelength. Earth's atmosphere scatters shorter blue wavelengths much more strongly than longer red wavelengths, so blue light is redirected across the sky from every direction. Redder light passes through more directly, which is why the sky looks blue while the sun itself appears more yellow or white.
